title: Council adopts 2026 budget with 2.2% tax increase
subtitle: No amendments proposed; Mayor did not use veto; staff directed to implement budget; conflicts declared on library and capital items.
overview: Kitchener City Council held a special meeting to finish approving the 2026 budget. Under provincial strong mayor legislation the Mayor proposes the budget, and Council's role at this meeting was to consider amendments. None were submitted by the December 8 deadline, and the Mayor said no veto would be used, so the budget was considered adopted.

Council then received the Mayor's Budget and directed staff to implement it {{vote:m1}}. The budget carries a 2.2% tax rate increase, which the minutes say amounts to about $29 a year for the average home. It funds existing services and capital work such as trails, parks, housing, tree canopy and the new Cowan Recreation Centre.

Four councillors declared conflicts on the library board budget and on specific capital projects. Those items were voted on separately and also carried unanimously. For residents, this means the 2026 tax rate and spending plan are settled and staff can begin carrying them out.

decisions.detail: Council received the Mayor's proposed 2026 Budget and directed staff to implement it, with the vote carried unanimously on a recorded vote {{vote:m1}}.

debate: Members of Council spoke in support of the budget and said the 2.2% increase keeps Kitchener's tax rate increases below inflation over the term and over the past decade.
One councillor said the budget does not rely on one-time funds, that reserves are healthy and that tax-supported debt is low and falling.
Several councillors compared the 2.2% increase with other municipalities, where they said increases are much higher and lead to deferred capital work or service cuts.
Speakers credited staff and a collaborative council: no amendments were brought for the third year in a row, and a councillor said experienced councillors and staff explain the consistency.
Highlights named included completing and opening the Cowan Recreation Centre, trail upgrades, housing investments, the tree canopy plan and community events funding.
